newsitem.title: USA: Rubin welcomes corporate tax change in Archer plan.
newsitem.headline: Rubin welcomes corporate tax change in Archer plan.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Wednesday that he was "gratified" by Republican plans to modify the proposed phase-out of the alternative minimum tax for large corporations.
But he questioned whether the extra revenues from such a move should be used to provide additional estate tax relief.

"Our inclination would be to put (the revenues) into provisions that most help middle and low income workers," Rubin told reporters. "I don't think it would have occured to me to put them into the estate tax."
House Speaker Newt Gingrich said earlier that House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer will propose changes to the estate tax provision in his bill that would "strengthen" the legislation.
Archer, a Texas Republican, had originally proposed gradually increasing the threshold where estate taxes kick in to $1 million by 2014 from the current $600,000.

Archer's new planned proposal would move $10 billion over 10 years from his proposed phase out of the corporate alternative minimum tax into the estate tax relief portion of his legislation, a committee aide said.
